_schema.why: one sentence: why this value, not what it is
_schema.evidence: where the number was measured/frozen (PREREG / csv / log)
_schema.class: algorithm = a record only, the engineer types it explicitly at launch (fool-proof rule); operational = launch scripts may read and apply it directly

rho.why: tier-1 eviction ratio 1/32: the only ratio measured flat in context length for constant-m schedules
rho.evidence: paper sec 'Recommended configuration'; PREREG curve legs

recall_capacity.why: recall fetch cap, per layer/request/decode step. A fixed buffer width, because CUDA graphs bake the shape in and a step is only as fast as its worst fetch; 4096 sits above the largest fire observed on the reference stack. The admission rule itself is uncapped (a row fires iff its certified score beats its own head's kept maximum, no top-k), so the cap sits behind the rule: a step that overflows attends the request's full row set, which is dense and exact. The cap is therefore spent in throughput and never in recall; the overflow rate is what the paper reports as the fallback rate. Flag: --vestigekv-recall-capacity. --disable-vestigekv-recall-overflow-fallback truncates instead and gives up the no-under-recall property. The per-head topj cap this entry used to describe is REMOVED from serving (SGLANG_VESTIGEKV_TOPJ is registered deprecated and ignored); it survives only in harness/e2e.py.

index_rank.why: tier-2 sketch rank r when the archive is GPU-resident (fetches cheap -> minimize scan bytes); use 192 under host offload (minimize triggers)

sinks.why: attention-sink rows always kept regardless of sigma

recent_window.why: NO LONGER A KEEP RULE. The deployed policy is sigma-top-m plus 4 sinks plus the UNCLOSED TAIL -- the up-to-one-block remainder of not-yet-closed rows, attended unconditionally -- and that tail subsumes the recent-window role; select_kept's contract is top-m by sigma plus sinks and nothing else. The constant survives only as the row-invariant checker's scale. Recorded so the 256-row window is not reintroduced as a policy.
recent_window.evidence: vestigekv/eviction.py select_kept docstring; vestigekv_mla_backend.py blockwise-sigma comment ('it subsumes the recent-window role')

attention_backend.why: the VestigeKV wrapper; wraps the Triton MLA backend on SM120 (flashinfer MLA JIT needs CUDA>=12.9 toolkit). Selecting this backend IS the enable switch: there is no SGLANG_ENABLE_VESTIGE knob, and the dense control arm is --attention-backend triton, which no env var can override
attention_backend.evidence: VESTIGEKV_PORT.md bring-up log; wrapper overhead measured at ~1% (triton 137.2 vs algorithm-off wrapper 138.6/139.9, S=64k bs=1, 2026-09-06)

sampling_backend.why: SM120: flashinfer sampling JIT fails its arch check and SIGQUITs the PP group at first generate; pytorch sampling is arch-agnostic and identical for greedy

pp_partition.why: largest KV pool (1,206,077 tokens, 2.3x the memory-driven 21/6) at equal decode speed - the two GB202 cards are near-equal, so the split only moves capacity

mem_fraction_static.why: leaves activation headroom for 8192-token chunked prefill on the 32GB rank; not re-tuned since bring-up
mem_fraction_static.evidence: bring-up (no sweep - arbitrary within a working range)

chunked_prefill_size.why: bounds the 5090's prefill activation at large S (65536 one-shot OOMed by 256MB)

context_length.why: curve/batch experiment config; capacity probes use 1048576 (pool shrinks to 525137 there)

nccl_env.why: cross-machine activation transport tuning: 14.6 Gbit/s on the eth0 link; metadata deliberately stays on gloo (its own CPU communicator off the CUDA stream - the NCCL-object experiment deadlocked and was reverted)

recall_tier.why: necessary at long context, and NOT closeable: the partition invariant is only meaningful if the archive is consulted, and with recall off the selector alone drops to 0.89 at 32x and 0.69 at 128x where both tiers recover every trial. The only knob is the fetch capacity (recall_capacity). The '99.8% per-step trigger at S=512k' this entry used to claim is REMOVED: its evidence pointed at PREREG31/32, which do not exist (the pre-registrations are prereg2..prereg10 and prereg_recall_margin), no measurement of it survives, and it contradicted the paper's own finding that a trigger firing on ~99.5% of steps is no compression at all while the adopted conformal trigger fires on 1.9%.
recall_tier.evidence: tier-1 ablation (paper Appendix 'Baseline behaviour on this model'); rule recorded 2026-09-06
